label: first copy step re-inputting a leading w in short sequences
explanation: Sparse feature (~0.03% of steps). 78% of activation mass is on the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx==1), where the input is the fed-back first original token. It is strongly selective for that token being w (65% of mass on in_tok w, lift 20x), with weaker firing for y and x. Activation is larger in short sequences (L=3,4 carry 67% of mass; rate falls off sharply for L>=6) and in sequences with no digits. Strongest examples are L=3 sequences starting with w (e.g. w r x <DEL> [w]). Even within that context the second original token matters: w followed by r/c/d/n/o/w fires, while w followed by h/e/p/f/b often does not, so precision is low (~0.3). The other ~21% of mass is weak, scattered firing in the original phase at positions 3-5 (late in short sequences, often after m/h/j or on w/y), and this predicate does not capture it. Never fires at t<3, on the delimiter step, or past recall_idx 2. Best simple predicate gets dev F1 ~0.37, mass recall ~0.48.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=4 (+4.92), orig_idx=3 (+4.85), prev_tok=m (+4.01), in_tok=y (+3.65), orig0=w (+3.50), t=5 (+3.42). Lower it: correct=1 (-7.56), orig1=j (-2.90), prev2_tok=c (-2.03), prev3_tok=- (-0.92).
